description: PSA model with temperature-dependent adsorption capacity and enhanced pressure/part-load corrections
source: Sircar & Golden (2000) Sep. Sci. Technol.; Yang (1987); Ruthven (1984) Principles of Adsorption; Cavenati et al. (2004) J. Chem. Eng. Data

specific_energy_kWh_per_kg_H2.note: Nominal specific energy per Sircar & Golden (2000)

energy_pressure_factor.note: W = W_nom*(P_ref/P)^0.15 per task specification (Sircar & Golden 2000)

Q_ads_H2.note: Isosteric heat of adsorption of H2 on activated carbon (~800 J/mol). Ruthven 1984

Q_ads_CO2.note: Isosteric heat of adsorption of CO2 on zeolite 5A (~25 kJ/mol). Cavenati 2004

E_a_cap.note: Apparent activation energy for adsorption capacity vs temperature. van't Hoff: q(T) = q_ref*exp(E_a/R*(1/T_ref - 1/T))

recovery_temp_coeff.note: Linear T-correction to recovery: eta = eta_base * (1 + k*(T - T_ref)). Higher T reduces adsorption selectivity. Sircar & Golden (2000)

energy_temp_exponent.note: Specific energy T-correction: W = W_base * (T/T_ref)^0.5. Higher T -> reduced adsorption -> more recompression needed.
